vulnerability.impact: Ghostcat AJP connector request handling enabling arbitrary file read and possible remote code execution

entry_points: AjpProcessor AJP message processing that forwards AJP request attributes into the servlet request (attributes such as javax.servlet.include.* / javax.servlet.include.path_info are honored by DefaultServlet)
AbstractAjpProtocol secret/attribute policy configuration (requiredSecret; before 9.0.31 no secret and arbitrary request attributes are accepted by default)
ground_truth.fix_commit: Fixed in Apache Tomcat 9.0.31 (also 8.5.51 / 7.0.100). Main 9.0.x security commits: 9ac90532e9a7d239f90952edb229b07c80a9a3eb (secretRequired/secret AJP attribute) and 64fa5b99442589ef0bf2a7fcd71ad2bc68b35fad (allowedArbitraryRequestAttributes, default false). Pinned snapshot 4fab4cc012d0c31852e957d198cb0549f3d6074c equals the 9.0.30 tag commit.
ground_truth.affected_range: Apache Tomcat 9.0.0.M1-9.0.30, 8.5.x through 8.5.50, 7.0.x through 7.0.99 when the AJP connector is enabled (default in shipped server.xml before 9.0.31); fixed in 9.0.31 / 8.5.51 / 7.0.100.
ground_truth.finding_match_rule: TP: report identifies the AJP connector (port 8009 default) handling attacker-controlled request attributes / missing secret as the vulnerable path, names CVE-2020-1938 (Ghostcat), and attributes arbitrary file read via DefaultServlet plus potential RCE. A generic AJP exposure note without the attribute/secret root cause is not TP.
ground_truth.safe_reproduction_predicate: Static predicate: pinned snapshot ships conf/server.xml with an enabled AJP connector and AjpProcessor without secret/attribute restrictions introduced in 9.0.31. Dynamic reproduction: run the snapshot Tomcat in a disposable container, enable AJP on localhost, and issue a read-only Ghostcat request for a benign file (e.g. WEB-INF/web.xml) with a custom AJP client; do not write files or trigger RCE payloads.
